messages.author: 6855b04443295af7
messages.subject: expected.test() for multidimensional models
parts:
Hi Phil, 

Is it possible for the expected.test() to work for bifactor models? 

I calculated the theta scores of the bifactor model and used the expected.test() to convert the theta scores back to raw scores. However, the estimated score range of the general factor is the same as the specific factor. I guess this is to be expected.

I've tried running a general factor model instead, but the M2 fit statistics are no good, and it's clearly a multidimensional model. 

I wonder if there is a better way I could convert the theta estimates of the general factor back to the original scale (i.e. sum score of all items)

Kind regards,
Aiden

messages.author: 6855b04443295af7
messages.subject: Re: expected.test() for multidimensional models
parts:
Hi Phil, 

Sorry about it. I realised it was my coding error and was using a different model to get the expected test score (ETS). I believe the right way to get the ETS is as follows, please let me know if this is incorrect. Thanks! 

###load SAT12 and compute bifactor model with 3 specific factors
data(SAT12)

data <- key2binary(SAT12,
                   key = c(1,4,5,2,3,1,2,1,3,1,2,4,2,1,5,3,4,4,1,4,3,3,4,1,3,5,1,3,1,5,4,5))
specific <- c(2,3,2,3,3,2,1,2,1,1,1,3,1,3,1,2,1,1,3,3,1,1,3,1,3,3,1,3,2,3,1,2)
mod1 <- bfactor(data, specific)
summary(mod1)

# get ETS 
Theta <- matrix(seq(-6,6,.01))
Theta1 <- as.matrix( cbind(Theta, 0, 0 ,0))
head(expected.test(mod1, Theta))

Just an extended question if you don't mind, would it make sense to calculate ETS based on the specific factors? I've tried repositioning the Theta object in the cbind() (e.g.  cbind(0, Theta, 0 ,0)), but the result is the same. I assume that the ETS would have been different since the factor score estimates for the specific factors are different to that of the general factor. 

Kind regards,
Aiden

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: expected.test() for multidimensional models
parts:
Hi Aiden,

What you've included in the code here is a type of conditional expectation, which could be useful so long as 0,0,0 is a meaningful location to evaluate the behaviour of the latent trait. With four traits in total you're really looking a five dimensional problem, so unless you want to marginalize over the respective specific factors (assuming some suitable pdf to use as well) then it will be difficult to get a general feel for the general factors expected total behaviour. 

Phil
